§6Poisonous Mud§f §aThe Watz Power Plant makes terrible power and even worse waste. That waste is your CMB Steel ingredient.§f §bPoisonous Mud§f is a strongly corrosive, polluting, radioactive viscous liquid (NFPA 4/0/3, ACID). It spews out of the §bWatz Power Plant§f during operation and can also be produced from depleted Watz pellets in a §bPUREX§f. §6Production§f:
§b• Watz Power Plant§f, continuous output during operation
§b• PUREX§f, depleted Watz pellets + kerosene + nitric acid §6Key Uses§f:
§b• §eCombine Steel§f, crucible: 6 nuggets of one metal + 3 nuggets of poisonous mud bricks → CMB Steel Ingot
§b• §eGas Centrifuge§f, 2 centrifuges produce dust, lead, iron, and tiny piles of nuclear waste
§b• §eIncinerate Excess§f, mud containers hold up to 64,000 mB for disposal §ePS:§f Don't throw away your poisonous mud. It's a valuable source of lead, iron, and the only way to get CMB Steel. Each Watz cycle produces significant quantities, so set up a processing pipeline early!
